summary: This diff adds a real, well-intentioned fix for the phase_4/PR#562 false-self-report incident: --audit-plans independently re-verifies every already-'done' phase against a real gh-confirmed merged PR and reverts (with a logged, committed incident) any that fail re-verification, and it is backed by a regression test that faithfully reproduces the real incident and passes. It correctly avoids the forbidden .github/workflows/** path, touches no auth/schema/migration/payment paths, and tier1 classification is appropriate for its blast radius on paper. However, confirm_merge() -- reused unchanged from the existing best-effort backfill path -- collapses 'confirmed NOT merged' and 'could not verify' (gh returncode != 0 from auth failure, rate limiting, transient network error, or a bad target_repo value) into the same False result, and find_first_unverified_done_block() treats any False as a violation. Since this is the exact same script that autonomously commits and pushes reverts directly to origin/master on a cron sweep with no human in the loop, a transient `gh` failure during any cron tick would cause it to auto-revert and push a permanently-recorded, factually false 'no real MERGED PR' incident for genuinely-completed, already-merged phases across every phase-plan file in the repo -- a worse failure mode than the bug it's meant to fix, since it converts silent under-detection into active data corruption of shared state. This is inconsistent with the diff's own handling of other verification failures (blame_line/parent-lookup failures correctly skip-with-warning rather than reverting), which shows the gh-failure path was simply missed rather than a deliberate tradeoff. There are secondary, non-blocking gaps worth follow-up: the audit silently skips (no incident, exit 0) any already-'done' phase whose plan file has no target_repo field at all (a real, already-existing plan file in this repo, AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-24.yaml, has zero target_repo fields across all phases, so this fix provides no coverage there despite the incident log's broad 'closes this gap' framing); and a wholly fabricated new phase block (not a modified existing one) has no parent revision to revert to, so it also silently skips with only a stderr warning and no incident recorded. Recommend fixing confirm_merge's ambiguous-failure handling (skip-and-warn on gh error/JSON-parse failure, only revert on a definitive non-merged state) before this is safe to auto-merge and run unattended.
issues: scripts/backfill_phase_self_report.py: confirm_merge() (reused by find_first_unverified_done_block) returns merged=False both when gh genuinely reports no merged PR AND when the gh call itself fails (non-zero returncode, JSON parse error) -- the audit path then treats any of these identically as a bypass violation and reverts + auto-commits + pushes to master. A transient gh auth/rate-limit/network failure during the cron sweep would cause false reverts of legitimately-merged, already-done phases, with a factually incorrect 'no real MERGED PR' message baked permanently into the master commit history.

scripts/backfill_phase_self_report.py: find_first_unverified_done_block() skips auditing any phase whose block has no target_repo field ('nothing to re-verify, never treated as a violation by absence alone') -- ai-os/AUDITOR_ENGINE_PHASE_PLAN_2026-07-24.yaml, a real existing plan file in this repo, has zero target_repo fields on any phase, so --audit-plans provides no real protection for that file's phases despite the module docstring and incident log both framing this as closing the general class of gap.

scripts/backfill_phase_self_report.py: audit_and_correct_plan_file() silently breaks (stderr warning only, no incident recorded, exit code 0, result['changed'] stays False) when blame_line() or the parent-revision phase lookup fails -- this includes the case of a worker fabricating an entirely new phase block from scratch (no prior 'not_started' state to revert to), arguably the most direct reproduction of the original bypass. The JSON audit output gives no visibility that a violation was found but left unfixed.

tests/backfill_phase_self_report_test.py: only exercises the single happy-path revert scenario; no coverage for a gh-call failure (should NOT revert), a target_repo-less plan file (should still be flagged as a known gap, or at least logged), or a from-scratch fabricated phase block (parent lookup failure path).
